questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As i was completing my bachelor project at the host university it was important that i was able to find a research project. Futher more i had visited Ireland before and really liked the atmosphere.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In hing sight the climate in ireland was a lot like the climate in Denmark, a bit dol and cold. If where to choose again I might look into somewhere that had a different and warmer climate.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine, most information however was sent out a little late, so you weren't really able to plan that much. Orientation also started before the semester ended at my home university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There where student guides that where accessible via the welcome desk, and an orientation program the first 2 weeks. There where also a course coordinator helping change any modules

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Over all the information came out late, sometimes the day before or even on the day so, wich made it hard to attend sometimes. Furthermore a lot of the activities where not that well executed.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorm room style housing, varying in number of rooms per apartment, some with ensuite bathrooms and some with shared bathrooms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
So most apartments where with out ovens, only equipped with stove and microwaves. You also need to supply kitchenware you slef including pots and pans. 
(Ovens where available in village apartments)

One house had catered food option.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It is way to expensive and poor quality but it is a great way to meet new people and make friends, some of my best friends from my semester abroad is from my apartment. 
Yes if an oven is important to you they are available in the village apartments, there is very little fridge space. Most of the shared bathrooms are only shared between two students and not amongst the hole apartment.

questions.answer: very successful, the harvest thing was to select subjects that did not overlap in lecture time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There are two types of course available XXXX3xxxx or XXXX4xxxx, (all courses are a 4 leter code corresponding to the field folwed by numbers, indicating the grade) the three indicates a third yer module, these where very brode and som courses had a big curriculum and i found these harder than the 4th year modules (which is their final year of the bachelor. the 4th year modules where mostly 4 week courses with smaller curriculums and was from my perspective easier to follow.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: very mush the same although mostly lectures and some lab exercise but not taught lessons where you do assignments in class. the third yare classes are open to more people so these where in larger lecture halls like A3 or A4. and 4th year classes where in smaller more classroom sized lecture rooms.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BMOL30050: Genomics and Proteomics
MIRC40060: Bioprocessing
BIOC40220: Hot topics in Biochemistry
BMOL40330: Biomol Sci. Research Project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BIOC40220: Hot topics in Biochemistry, interesting course where you lean how to better communicate science. low effort course with 4-5 lectures and 4 assignments taking an evening each and if you wright the professor and ask they can basically be on any topic in the field of molecular biology.

MIRC40060: Bioprocessing, this was a very interesting module where we learned about production of protein and penicillin and more from cells in large scale bioreactors. (medium to hard effort) 

BMOL40330: Biomol Sci. Research Project (mandatory for BA farmaci KU studerende, this is the Bachelor Project)

the PI food shop in science east is very good and okay prices, very good breakfast
set a goal of going out to explore something once or twice a week and have a list with thing you want to go do, and plan these things in advance. i did not see that much stuff because i ran out of time on my exchange
